BannerCell.description:
A text above the header row, merged over columns ``first`` to ``last``
(1 is A), as the template prints its title and its group labels.
BannerCell.title: BannerCell

UploadColumn.description:
One column of the upload file, at its place in the template, and where
its value comes from: a field code computes from the case, an attribute of
the customer's master record, or a fixed text; none of the three, and the
column is blank for the person who pastes (ticket 02: a column change is
data, never code). ``number_format`` is the template's own format for the
column's cells; without one a value prints as it is held.
UploadColumn.title: UploadColumn

sales_bravo_upload.description:
``configs/policies/sales_bravo_upload@<version>.yaml``.

Schema 1.0 (the mock layouts 1.0.0 and 1.1.0) is a header row and the
fields under it. Schema 2.0 (B41, ticket 02) is the template as Bravo's
"Import Sales Order" prints it: the rows above the header row
(``banner``, an empty row for a row with nothing on it), then the header
row, each column at its place with its source, then a row per delivery.
A 1.0 document has no rows above its headers: one read over a 2.0
platform version (`read_over`) is not given the platform's.
sales_bravo_upload.title: BravoUploadLayout

EmailAddress.description: One mailbox: an address and the name shown beside it.
EmailAddress.title: EmailAddress

SenderPolicy.description:
Who a customer draft is from, until Proterial answers (requirements
doc §3.1): ``drafting_pic`` is the address of the PIC who drafts it and
sends it from their own mailbox; ``shared_sales`` the shared address.
Reply-To is always the shared Sales address.
SenderPolicy.title: SenderPolicy

ImpliedAcceptanceRule.description:

records the agreement. DW1 never records it.

MorningBrief.description:

DesignRequestTemplate.description:
The words of the request Sales sends Design to create a PRV code for a
line no item fits (ticket 06), from the order case: ``{customer}``,
``{po}``, ``{line_no}``, ``{customer_item}``, ``{description}`` (as the PO
prints it), ``{quantity}``, ``{uom}``, ``{requested_date}`` and
``{nearest}`` in the subject and body; one ``nearest`` per code of the
tenant's item master nearest the line, with ``{code}`` and its
``{description}``, or ``no_nearest`` where none is.
DesignRequestTemplate.title: DesignRequestTemplate

HandoffTemplate.description:
One kind's words. Placeholders are filled by code from the hand-off:
``{customer}``, ``{po}``, ``{message_id}``, ``{lines}``, ``{lot}``,
``{quotes}``, ``{quantity}``.
HandoffTemplate.title: HandoffTemplate

PcRequestTemplate.description:
The words of the request Sales sends PC for an order's delivery dates
(ticket 07), from the order case: ``{customer}``, ``{po}``, ``{lines}``
in the subject and body, one ``line`` per line asked with ``{line_no}``,
``{item}`` (the PRV code), ``{customer_item}``, ``{quantity}``,
``{uom}`` and ``{requested_date}``.
PcRequestTemplate.title: PcRequestTemplate

StepId.description:
The surveyed steps' ids as a closed set: what a value kept per step (the
KPI's manual baseline) is keyed by, so a version written before a step was
surveyed reads that step as the platform has it (`rules.read_over`). Held
to `WIV_STEPS`, which owns the steps themselves, by a test.
StepId.title: StepId

sales_kpi.description:
What the overview measures against.

``order_confirmation_target_hours``: from the PO's arrival to the order
confirmed. ``quotation_target_days``: from the request's arrival to the
quotation sent (1, Đạt 2026-10-05). ``manual_baseline_minutes``: what one
pass of each surveyed step (O1 … Q12) takes by hand today, the column the
per-step export carries beside its counts. Every surveyed step is listed:
a step without a baseline would export as if it took no time. Keyed by
`StepId`, a closed set, so a version written before a step was surveyed
is read with the platform's baseline for it, and a key the survey does
not have is refused.
sales_kpi.title: SalesKpi

Autonomy.description:
How much error a step that applies its result by itself may make
(dw_sales ADR 0015, decided 2026-11-16; ticket 44). The tier of each step
is code's (`dw_sales.domain.autonomy.STEP_TIERS`); these are the
tenant's numbers for each tier that may apply itself. A tenant may only
tighten them: the upper bounds are the platform's defaults, so loosening
one is a platform change.
Autonomy.title: Autonomy

FindingCode.description: The order checks of the spec's findings table, one code each.
FindingCode.title: FindingCode

ImpliedTerm.description:
A customer's silence that counts as agreement: after this many days,
counted this way, from that day (the order rules' `implied_acceptance`,
one per customer, none by default).
ImpliedTerm.title: ImpliedTerm

IntakeCaps.description: How much of a sender's file a reader opens before refusing it (decision 13).
IntakeCaps.title: IntakeCaps

LayoutOnboarding.description: How a newly approved PO layout earns trust (ticket 30).
LayoutOnboarding.title: LayoutOnboarding

Learning.description:
How DW1's readings learn from what people decided (dw_sales ADR 0015
decision 5, ticket 43). Numbers only: what is shown and what is proposed
is code's to choose, and a proposed prompt version is the head's to
approve.
Learning.title: Learning

ModelAssist.description:
Which DW1 steps a model takes part in for the tenant (dw_sales ADR 0005).

Each is a switch the platform ships off; a tenant turns one on in its own
version of these rules. The case stamps the version it was checked under,
so what a case was read with never changes after.
ModelAssist.title: ModelAssist

Severity.description: ``error`` is blocking; ``warning`` is shown. Both need a decision.
Severity.title: Severity

sales_order_rules.description:
`sales_order_rules`: the fine print of the order checks, versioned.

Every finding code has a severity, and a policy that leaves one out is
refused: a code with no severity would be a check whose result blocks
nothing, which reads as a safeguard and is not one.
sales_order_rules.title: OrderRules

CopperAdder.description: What is added to LME copper while LME is inside ``band``, in USD per tonne.
CopperAdder.title: CopperAdder

FreightRate.description: Freight for one incoterm to one destination, per kilometre of cable.
FreightRate.title: FreightRate

LmeBand.description: The price holds while LME copper is in ``[low, high)`` USD per tonne.
LmeBand.title: LmeBand

ReferenceRule.description:
How the quote policy forms a reference price, and the band around it.

The reference is the mean of the prices the item is quoted at on the day,
to any customer, in the request's currency, counting a price tied to an
LME band only while the month's LME is inside that band. It is rounded to
the precision those prices are quoted in, and the band is rounded inwards,
so rounding never widens it.
ReferenceRule.title: ReferenceRule

sales_quote_rules.description:
The quote policy: `configs/policies/sales_quote_rules@<version>.yaml`.

Whoever loads the file validates it here, so every version passes the
same checks before any of it is applied.
sales_quote_rules.title: QuoteRules

BriefWords.description:
The morning brief's counts, a title and three lines. ``{day}`` the
brief's day, ``{since}`` the previous brief's slot, ``{whose}`` the
`workspace` or `mine` words, ``{waiting}`` the counts per whom the cases
wait on (`waits_on`, else `nothing`); every other placeholder a count.
BriefWords.title: BriefWords

HoursReminder.description: As `SinceReminder`, and ``{hours}``: the tenant's threshold in hours.
HoursReminder.title: HoursReminder

NextSteps.description:
What the person does next on their turn, where DW1 did the step before
it: said in the reminder (and told to the brief's writer), so nobody has
to open the case to learn it. No placeholder.
NextSteps.title: NextSteps

PushWords.description:
What a push says (ticket 48): the kind of work, never a customer, a
price or their text. No placeholder but the batch's ``{count}``; the
case's number follows `order` or `quote` where the tenant allows it.
PushWords.title: PushWords

ReminderWords.description:
One reminder per follow-up, and per way it reads (`followups.Followup`;
which one a case gets is code's, `followups.reminder_text`).
ReminderWords.title: ReminderWords

SinceReminder.description:
``{ref}`` the case's number, ``{customer}`` its customer code,
``{since}`` when the wait began (local time).
SinceReminder.title: SinceReminder

ColumnRule.description:
One column of the upload file, by its letter in the tenant's layout:
where its value starts (a field of the normal reading, or the customer's
record; none only where the first step is a constant) and the steps it
then goes through, in order.
ColumnRule.title: ColumnRule

Concat.description: Appends the values of other fields, each after the separator.
Concat.title: Concat

Constant.description: The value is this fixed text.
Constant.title: Constant

Copy.description: Keeps the value as it is.
Copy.title: Copy

CustomerSalesOrderRules.description: One customer's columns: each named once.
CustomerSalesOrderRules.title: CustomerSalesOrderRules

Cut.description:
Keeps the characters from ``start`` to before ``end`` (from 0; a
negative number counts from the end; none: the start or the end).
Cut.title: Cut

Lookup.description:
The value is what the master data's table holds for it, or for the
field ``key`` where one is named.
Lookup.title: Lookup

Multiply.description: Multiplies the value by another field's.
Multiply.title: Multiply

ShiftDays.description: Moves a date by whole calendar days.
ShiftDays.title: ShiftDays

UnitFactor.description: Multiplies the value by how many ``to`` make one ``from``.
UnitFactor.title: UnitFactor

sales_salesorder_rules.description:
``sales_salesorder_rules``: the tenant's customers' rules, by customer
code. The platform ships none; every customer's arrives as a tenant
version learned from a worked example and approved.
sales_salesorder_rules.title: SalesOrderRules
